summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, and chronic left index finger wound due to steal syndrome was admitted with worsening pain, fevers, and signs of infection. Imaging revealed osteomyelitis and soft tissue infection, leading to a left index finger ray amputation and tendon transfer. Blood and wound cultures grew E. coli, sensitive to ertapenem. He was treated with IV antibiotics, initially meropenem, and transitioned to outpatient IV ertapenem via a PICC line for a six-week course. His acute kidney injury resolved with hydration, and his blood pressure and glucose levels were managed with continued home medications. The patient improved clinically, with a clean incision and stable vitals, and was discharged home with wound care instructions, pain management, and follow-up plans with hand surgery and infectious disease.
